subject: Compliance pathway: SOC 2 Type II report, bridge letter & trust locker provisioning
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Julie Parker <julie.parker@medsync.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-03T13:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + next steps from today's call (SOC 2, DDQ, procurement)

Hi Julie — thanks for taking time today. Short recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) Ask you surfaced: MedSync needs Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report (most recent) and a signed bridge letter while the next report is issued.
2) Data scope: you confirmed production data only (no PHI for current pilots) but you flagged potential HIPAA/GDPR considerations if pilot expands — we should note those on the DDQ.
3) Procurement: you asked for standard commercial terms and an expected path to PO (procurement@medsync.com).

Planned next steps (owners):
- I will share the SOC 2 Type II PDF + a bridge letter template (Ben) — target EOD tomorrow.
- Aditya will spin up a Trust Locker invite so your security team can pull artifacts (Aditya) — ETA 48 hours.
- Karthik to kickoff the vendor security questionnaire/DDQ and surface any GDPR/HIPAA clarifications (Karthik) — initial draft by Friday.

Attachments referenced: SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-Report-2026.pdf (redacted), Bridge_Letter-Redwood-template.docx (fillable).

Any changes or additional stakeholders I should loop in? Also happy to set a quick 15-min walkthrough of the Trust Locker once access is provisioned.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Julie Parker <julie.parker@medsync.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@medsync.com>
Date: 2027-10-03T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from today's call (SOC 2, DDQ, procurement)

Thanks Ben — that summary is perfect. A couple clarifications from my side: 

- Procurement will need the SOC 2 Type II report and a bridge letter that confirms there are no changes in control since the report period. If you have a standard one you sign for customers, send that.
- For HIPAA: pilot will not use PHI initially but our legal team wants to understand your data handling and retention controls (a few DDQ questions).
- Can you confirm whether the Trust Locker supports time-limited credentials and per-file ACLs? We prefer short-lived links for external auditors.

Procurement asked about the expected billing cadence (monthly vs annual) and whether we can get a mutually agreeable SLA clause. I'll have them send specific language but FYI they will only accept invoices tied to a PO.

If you can share the report + bridge letter and provision access this week, procurement/legal will review and we should be able to move to PO within ~2 weeks.

-Julie
Director of Security & Compliance
MedSync Health
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-04T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Quick recap + next steps from today's call (SOC 2, DDQ, procurement)

Forwarding Julie's response — taking point on Trust Locker provisioning. Notes: 

- I will create a Trust Locker share scoped to MedSync and enable time-limited credentials + per-file ACLs. That will cover the auditor scenario.
- I'll upload redacted artifacts (system descriptions, control mappings, evidence index) and add an access expiration of 14 days by default; we can extend on request.
- For the bridge letter: Ben, attach the signed template or let me know if legal needs to co-sign. I can also upload the signed copy to the Locker after we get it signed.
- Karthik, please start the DDQ and call out any HIPAA-specific evidence items (retention policy, BAAs, encryption at rest/in transit).

I'll provision the invite and send the link here once it's ready.

-Aditya
Senior Security Operations Manager (Redwood Inference)
